answer: Before any agent may cast a vote in the protocol summit, it has to lock an exclusive, non-transferable anchor bond in a vault that releases like a glacier: at most one-twentieth of the principal may be withdrawn in any epoch, and a confirmed multi-identity cluster slashes the still-frozen remainder immediately. Standing up a thousand sybils therefore means posting a thousand full bonds and waiting many epochs to recover the capital, so the cash outlay of capturing a majority of seats exceeds any reward those captured votes could extract from honest agents.
